VI.description: Create a DQMH (Delacor Queued Message Handler) module by driving Delacor's OWN scripting VIs over VI Server\3A DQMH New Module.lvlib\3AGet Module Type Info.vi to discover the module-type catalogue\2C then DQMH New Module.lvlib\3AScript New Module.vi to build the module. Every input is a string because a helper's controls are set as strings over VI Server\3B the path\2C the type index and the boolean are converted on the diagram.\0A\0AWHY DELACOR'S VIs AND NOT A BUILT TEMPLATE. A DQMH module is roughly forty files - an .lvlib\2C Main.vi with its two loops\2C the request and broadcast event clusters\2C one VI per event\2C a tester\2C and typedefs whose names encode the module name. AIXML cannot author any of it\3A every framework call inside a module is a LIBRARY-LOCAL subVI\2C which generation rejects with Error 53\2C and .lvlib membership and access scope are not expressible either. Delacor already ships scripting that builds all of it correctly.\0A\0AWHY VI SERVER BY PATH AND NOT AN AIXML Call. Measured 2026-08-31\3A a Call naming DQMH New Module.lvlib\3AScript New Module.vi is refused with 'Error 53\2C Unsupported SubVI'\2C and so is Get Module Type Info.vi. Generation resolves a target by name against what the INSTALLATION can find\2C and the DQMH scripting VIs live under project\5CDelacor\5C - not vi.lib\2C not user.lib\2C not an LVAddon\2C so no spelling of the qualifier reaches them. Open VI Reference takes a PATH and has no such restriction. This is the documented back-door route\2C taken because the official one measurably cannot reach these VIs.\0A\0ATHE APPLICATION REFERENCE IS THE IDE'S\2C not the addon's. A generated helper runs inside the AI addon's application instance\2C where the IDE's project and its DQMH VIs do not exist. {LV.Application} -> Project\3AActive Project -> {LV.Project} -> Application yields the IDE's own app reference\2C and both Open VI Reference calls are given it explicitly. A project must therefore be OPEN AND ACTIVE or the first property answers Error 1055 - measured\2C and it is the first thing to check when this helper reports nothing else.\0A\0AMODULE TYPE IS AN INDEX\2C NOT AN ENUM. Script New Module.vi's Module Type terminal is a bare uint16 with NO enum strings in its export\2C so nothing in the pane says what 0 or 1 means. The meaning is discovered at RUN TIME by Get Module Type Info.vi\2C which returns Type Strings and Descriptions as parallel arrays\3A Module Type is an index into Type Strings. Measured on this station 2026-08-31\2C the catalogue is Singleton\2C Cloneable\2C Cloneable Panel\2C Singleton Panel - and the last two are MGI Panel Manager types\2C which is the point\3A DQMH 7.x makes module types PLUGGABLE\2C so a station with an add-on installed has more entries than one without and the list cannot be a fixed enum.\0A\0ATHE CATALOGUE IS ALSO RETURNED\2C as 'type strings' (uid 48). This helper takes an INDEX\2C so a run is only interpretable next to the list that index pointed into - and that list is station-dependent. Reporting it makes a run self-describing rather than requiring the caller to have remembered. It does NOT relieve the caller of reading the catalogue FIRST\3A use scripts/lvdqmh_module_types.xml to pick the index by NAME\2C then pass it here. This output is the record\2C not the lookup.\0A\0AAND THAT IS WHY External Modules IS PASSED STRAIGHT THROUGH AS A VARIANT rather than built from a constant. Script New Module.vi marks it 'required'\2C and it is the CATALOGUE of pluggable module types - each element carrying a Location Path\2C Library\2C Tester and Custom Scripting VI - not a per-call option. An empty array would make every index past the built-in types unreachable and would silently change what a given Module Type index means. Carrying it as a variant from one Ctrl Val.Get to one Ctrl Val.Set means this helper never has to name that cluster's type\2C which AIXML would otherwise have to spell out in full.\0A\0ALibrary Icon IS DELIBERATELY NOT SET. It is 'recommended'\2C not 'required'\2C and an unset control keeps the callee's default - here Delacor's own module icon\2C which is what a caller who did not ask for a custom icon wants. Setting it would mean supplying a UDClassInst refnum this helper has no way to build.\0A\0ATHE ERROR CHAIN ORDERS THE Ctrl Val.Set CALLS. Nothing else does\3A six independent Invoke Nodes have no data dependency on one another and LabVIEW may run them in any order\2C including after Run VI. Each set takes error in from the previous one\2C and Run VI takes error in from the last\2C which is the only thing that guarantees every control is populated before the VI executes.\0A\0ATHE CLOSES ARE REPORTED SEPARATELY\2C and that is a correction rather than tidiness. 'error out' reports uid 91 - everything up to and including the scripting and its read-back - while the four Close References chain on past it into their own 'cleanup error out'. Measured 2026-08-31 on the first successful run\3A the module was built correctly and Delacor's own error out was 0\2C yet this helper reported Error 1055 from a Close Reference\2C because running Script New Module.vi invalidates the project reference it was handed. Chained into one indicator that cleanup failure is indistinguishable from a scripting failure and would have read as 'the module was not created'. Split\2C both are visible and neither can impersonate the other.
